title: Netherlands name World Cup squad: Virgil van Dijk leads team, no place for Jeremie Frimpong
author: Sam Joseph
content:
Netherlands head coach Ronald Koeman has named his 26-man squad for this summer’s World Cup.

Captain Virgil van Dijk will lead the side this summer but there is no space for his Liverpool team-mate Jeremie Frimpong after an injury-plagued first season at Anfield.

There is a strong Premier League presence in the side, with 15 members of the squad playing their club football in England’s top flight.

Liverpool have two further players included, with midfielder Ryan Gravenberch and forward Cody Gakpo receiving call-ups. Brighton & Hove Albion are another team to be represented by a trio of players, with goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen, centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke and the versatile Mats Wieffer all included.

Manchester City’s Nathan Ake and Tijjani Reijnders have been named, as has Arsenal’s Jurrien Timber, who has not played since March due to a groin injury.

Tottenham Hotspur defender Micky van de Ven has been selected but his team-mate Xavi Simons is not included, having suffered an anterior cruciate ligament tear in April. Mathijs de Ligt is also absent through injury after undergoing surgery for a back injury earlier this month. The Manchester United defender has not played since November.

The Netherlands have reached the World Cup final three times (in 1974, 1978 and 2010) but are yet to win the competition. Koeman’s side begin their Group F campaign against Japan on June 14 before taking on Sweden on June 20 and Tunisia on June 25.

Analysis by Liverpool correspondent Gregg Evans

This will feel like another cruel blow for Frimpong who has had a season to forget.

Missing out on the squad was not even a thought when he joined Liverpool a year ago, following three and a half successful seasons at Bayer Leverkusen.

At that point, he was a big part of the Netherlands’ set-up and firmly focused on making an impact in this summer’s World Cup.

But a rotten run of injuries has derailed his progress, and ultimately it’s those setbacks that have cost him a place on the plane.

Frimpong was supposed to be a durable, versatile right-sided player who could give Liverpool plenty of options this season, but he’s struggled to make an impact at all.

Not only did he start just 12 games in the Premier League, he also picked up three hamstring injuries across the campaign and had to be managed carefully in the closing months to avoid another breakdown.

Given his lack of time on the pitch and the struggles he’s faced recently, it’s no great surprise that he’s missed out, but that’s not to say it won’t hurt.

At 25 years old, time is still on his side, but this knock back will sting for some time.

Analysis by football writer Carl Anka

Koeman’s squad prioritises functionality over creative improvisation. Many wondered how the head coach would respond to losing PSV captain Jerdy Schouten and Tottenham Hotspur’s Xavi Simons to ACL injuries, and whether he would opt for Feyenoord’s Luciano Valente or AZ’s Kees Smit as midfield alternatives to the expected midfield trio of Frenkie de Jong, Ryan Gravenberch and Tijjani Reijnders.

Koeman decided to pick … neither Valente nor Smit, instead favouring the seniority of Marten de Roon and Quinten Timber — the twin brother of Arsenal defender Jurrien, who is also in the squad.

Inter Milan centre-back Stefan de Vrij and Liverpool’s Frimpong are other notable omissions in a squad full of names familiar to Premier League viewers, but perhaps lacking the sort of star quality necessary to progress further than the quarter-finals.

Frimpong’s omission will have a knock-on effect for Donyell Malen. The forward has been in electric form for Roma following his January move from Aston Villa, a loan deal that was made permanent this week. Malen scored 15 goals in 20 appearances as a centre-forward for Roma, but may instead feature as a right winger at the World Cup as Koeman continues to build around Memphis Depay, who remains the Netherlands’ record top scorer.

Goalkeepers: Bart Verbruggen (Brighton), Robin Roefs (Sunderland), Mark Flekken (Bayer Leverkusen).

Defenders: Jurrien Timber (Arsenal), Micky van de Ven (Tottenham), Virgil van Dijk (Liverpool), Nathan Ake (Manchester City), Jorrel Hato (Chelsea), Denzel Dumfries (Inter ), Jan Paul van Hecke (Brighton).

Midfielders: Ryan Gravenberch (Liverpool), Tijjani Reijnders (Manchester City), Frenkie de Jong (Barcelona), Teun Koopmeiners (Juventus), Marten de Roon (Atalanta), Quinten Timber (Marseille), Guus Til (PSV Eindhoven), Mats Wieffer (Brighton).

Forwards: Brian Brobbey (Sunderland), Memphis Depay (Corinthians), Cody Gakpo (Liverpool), Justin Kluivert (Bournemouth), Noa Lang (Galatasaray), Donyell Malen (Roma), Crysencio Summerville (West Ham), Wout Weghorst (Ajax).
